cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Compare the angry letter with the one I sent. Notice the crossing-out. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology you sent. Why show me the angry version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Because 'sorry' took ten minutes. Not sending the rest took all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I'm tempted to read what you spared me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please admire the thickness with it shut. I'd like one night's restraint to survive breakfast.

mechanism: A manages a demonstration of restraint, adjusting how much of an angry letter B may inspect to retain recognition without undoing the apology.
confusable: Unlike wanting praise for a successful apology alone, A wants the effort of not sending the anger recognized; authority bargains over the demonstration.
comparison: Private restraint toward the apology recipient differs from an outgoing chair defending a hard-won refusal.
seedUse: Use D105-a unsent anger versus apology; S02-b accommodates B demand while maintaining a workable directed encounter.
